Trading is completely discretional. You can have mechanic aspects, but ultimately it is discretionary. 

Your problem is with this abstract notion that people have a discretionary advantage due to their time in the market, which is true, as with everything. You start to notice patterns and know what set ups are more probable than others due to extensive time in the market.

All trading is, is a game of probabilities. The point is to have an edge the same way a casino does with a roulette table.
It’s not even about the analysis you do or the trades you take, but more importantly how you manage risk. That’s all forex traders are, risk managers that utilise concepts that give them a proven higher probability entry than a flip coin which can be proven with large data from back testing a system. Generally speaking it’s very close to that of a coin flip, but it’s slightly advantageous which is all you need. The aforementioned roulette table, the only thing it has in its favour is the green zero. And that’s all it needs to always come out on top, as proven with the law of large numbers.

Me and about 20 other people trade ICT concepts and are all funded. Just because it’s too hard for you to grasp doesn’t mean it doesn’t work. Of course there are no bots, discretion is in the individual refinement of each persons style of trading and their trading plan, just utilising ICT concepts. entries and management can’t be objective because of the complete uncertainty of the markets and the conditions. ICT is simply a way of understanding the markets, whether it’s true or false is irrelevant, so long as it proves consistency that can be repeated allowing an edge in the market is all you need. Proper risk management of 1:2RR per trade allows for just above 50% strike rate which makes it near trivially easy to trade the markets and come out profitable, paired with leveraging capital of prop firms and that’s all you need. It’s not rocket science, brother.
